expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No. The test you added would have passed all three weeks.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: COALESCE(x, 0) turns those nulls into a legal-looking value. The pipeline had no way to fail.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Daily reconciliation: warehouse revenue total vs. billing source, per day. Only 'does it agree?' catches a wrong join.

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: build to staging → assert → promote. If assertions run after publish, bad data reaches the dashboard, which was the whole failure.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: Ingest contract on the upstream table — validate schema, quarantine to a dead-letter table

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Assert join-key match rate on staging (orphan rows = 0), promote only on pass

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Why nothing caught it: you had no reconciliation—identifies the gap in detection mechanism but does not specifically mention or address the 'three weeks' timeframe

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: convert a loud failure into a quiet wrong answer... undetectable downstream—describes that it's silent and undetectable, but does not explain why that is worse than a pipeline failure or what consequences follow from silence
